name: Stahlhandel Rupprecht-Kessel GmbH
summary: Stahlhandel Rupprecht-Kessel is a family-owned steel stockholder founded in 1908, with 500 staff and EUR 196 M turnover, sound finances and a stable credit index of 177. The owner deals with us personally and has twice offered to open his calculation. On 2026-09-16 he proposed a new price basis for sheet part:370020 with a PPI-C241 price adjustment clause, just ahead of the 2026-12-31 contract end and its 60-day notice deadline.
negotiation_pattern: It has always settled below its own opening ask, on average 2.37 pp lower (mean ask -2.95 %, mean settled -5.32 %). It even opened with cuts in 2023 (-5.9 % / -9.4 %, settled -9.1 % / -11.7 %). In 2024 it asked +1.5 % on part:370012 and settled flat. In 2025 it asked 0 % / -0.8 % and settled -2.3 % on both parts. It is cooperative and transparency-minded: the owner offered open-book costing (hourly rates and material) twice. It now wants to move from fixed annual prices to an index clause.
wants: Index clause on PPI-C241 for part:370020 (material risk pass-through)
Fair, respectful treatment and on-time payment (we pay late in 82 % of cases)
Long-term relationship and reference-customer status with Hollerau
Volume security / more share on part:370012 (holds only 40 %; its 2025 RFQ quote was not awarded)
protects: Material cost risk: wants index pass-through instead of a fixed annual price
unit_price below its calculation; it will defend with open-book data
payment_days (30 net, no skonto, no sign of interest in trading it)

trades.get: Symmetric clause (decreases passed through too), a defined material share with deadband, and a lower base unit_price set at today's index level
trades.why: This is its current ask; we only make it neutral by insisting on symmetry and a reset base.

trades.give: volume_per_year: raise quota on part:370012 above 40 %
trades.get: unit_price reduction on part:370012 and on-time-delivery improvement toward the 95 % target
trades.why: It quoted for more business in 2025 and lost; a loyalty-minded family firm values more share.

trades.give: contract_months: renew the framework for 24 months
trades.get: Price hold or reduction on both parts and a formal lead_time_days commitment of 10
trades.why: A steady long-term commitment is what an owner-led firm rewards.

trades.give: Pay strictly on the 30-day due date (stop late payments)
trades.get: Goodwill on price and acceptance of a symmetric index clause
trades.why: We pay late 82 % of the time; fixing that costs us little and builds trust.

arguments.point: Accept the owner's offer to walk through the calculation and set the price basis on open-book figures.
An index clause is only fair if it works both ways and starts from a base agreed today.
Hollerau is its stated reference customer. A long-term, steady partnership is on offer if terms are fair.
OTD of 92.2 % is still below the 95 % contractual target, so there is room to ask for a delivery commitment.
Our spend fell from EUR 486k to EUR 441k. More share on part:370012 is available for a competitive price.

avoid: Hard pressure or threats of resourcing: the owner remembers treatment and has been cooperative
Ignoring the index-clause letter or stalling past the notice deadline
Accepting a one-sided index clause (increases only) or one without a defined material share and base
Claiming leverage from our size: we are only 0.2 % of its turnover
Raising complaints aggressively: quality is green and improving
tone: Personal, respectful, partnership-oriented. Address the owner directly, thank him for the open-book offer and argue with facts.
red_flags: Contract ends 2026-12-31 and extends automatically. Notice and price-change deadlines are 60 days before year end, i.e. about 2026-11-01.
part:370020 is single source (100 %, no other source); a steel index clause exposes us to rising material prices.
Low dependency on us (0.2 % of turnover): it can walk away from a bad deal more easily than we can.
OTD 92.2 % is still below the 95 % target; one 8D is open (last complaint 2026-09-11).
Our chronic late payment (82 % of invoices) could sour the relationship.

evidence.claim: Family-owned, founded 1908, 500 staff, EUR 196 M turnover, equity ratio 39 %, credit index 177 (unchanged from 12 months ago): no cash stress.
The owner personally offered to walk us through hourly rates and material, twice.
It proposes a new price basis with a PPI-C241 adjustment clause for part:370020.
Last renewal settled at -2.3 % on both parts versus asks of 0 % and -0.8 %.
Contract runs to 2026-12-31, renews by 12 months automatically, 60-day notice; prices are fixed per calendar year.
Scorecard green for four quarters; OTD rose from 90.0 to 92.2 %, ppm at 44, score 95.9.
Sole source for sheet part:370020; holds 40 % of part:370012, with one other source.
Its 2025 RFQ quote for part:370012 at EUR 129.78/100 was not awarded; the current price is EUR 126.05/100.
It calls Hollerau an important reference customer.

indicators.credit_index: 177 (12 months ago 177; higher is worse, >300 weak)
indicators.scorecard_trend: 2025Q4 green (otd 90.0, ppm 56) → 2026Q1 green (otd 90.2, ppm 45) → 2026Q2 green (otd 90.6, ppm 32) → 2026Q3 green (otd 92.2, ppm 44)
